title: SharePoint forms: Power Automate trigger "When a form is submitted" and action "Get form metadata"
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap record and Microsoft documentation. The data-policy path, PowerShell command, licensing prerequisites and preview qualifications are accurate; no correction is required.

claims.claim: This is the SharePoint forms Power Automate integration described by roadmap item 561025 for Microsoft 365, Power Automate and SharePoint.
claims.quote: "title": "SharePoint: Power Automate trigger and action for forms in SharePoint"; "products": ["Microsoft 365", "Power Automate", "SharePoint"]

claims.claim: The SharePoint connector has a trigger named When a form is submitted.
claims.quote:
### When a form is submitted

Triggers a flow when a form in SharePoint is submitted.

claims.claim: The trigger supports list forms, file upload forms and document generation forms.
claims.quote: Supported form types include list forms, file upload forms, and document generation forms.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Users creating and configuring document generation forms need an assigned Microsoft Copilot licence.

claims.claim: Submission triggers the configured flow without a separate manual flow start.
claims.quote: Use this trigger to start a Power Automate flow when a supported form in SharePoint receives a response.

claims.claim: Power Automate does not apply form conditional visibility.
claims.quote: Power Automate doesn't apply conditional visibility: if you generate documents through a Power Automate flow, the flow doesn't hide or show fields the way the form does

claims.claim: A required field hidden by the form remains visible in a document generated through a flow.
claims.quote: so a required field that your form hides will still be visible in the document.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises making fields normally hidden by the form optional when using Power Automate.
claims.quote: When you use a form with Power Automate, make any field you'd normally hide an optional field so it doesn't block the intended flow.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The documented path is Power Platform admin center > Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Prebuilt connectors > SharePoint > Move to Business.
claims.quote: Select Security ... under Settings, select Data and privacy ... Data policy ... select a policy, and then select Edit Policy ... Select the Prebuilt connectors step ... select the Salesforce and SharePoint connectors, and then select Move to Business

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy GUID> -Classification Confidential -Connectors <connector objects> moves connectors into the policy's Business group.
claims.quote: Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively). ... -PolicyName: The policy name (GUID). ... -Connectors: The list of connectors to add to the policy.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; summary; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing environment-scoped data policies govern which connectors flows can combine with SharePoint.
claims.quote: By moving the Salesforce and SharePoint connectors to the Business data group, you're preventing users from creating flows and apps that combine these two connectors with any of the connectors in the Non-business or Blocked groups.

claims.claim: SharePoint is not blockable, so its Block action is unavailable in data policies.
claims.quote: For connectors like SharePoint that aren't blockable, the Block action isn't available and a warning appears.

claims.claim: Connector action control allows or blocks individual actions and triggers but cannot be configured for unblockable connectors such as SharePoint.
claims.quote: You can use connector action control to allow or block individual actions or triggers within a given connector. ... You can configure connector actions for all blockable connectors, but not for unblockable connectors and custom connectors.

claims.claim: The documented tenant-level policy procedure requires the Power Platform Administrator role.
claims.quote: To follow the steps described in this article for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: Environment-level policies require Environment Admin permissions, subject to the Dataverse exception.
claims.quote: To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions.

claims.claim: Environments with a Dataverse database require the System Administrator role instead.
claims.quote: For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.claim: Environment admins cannot edit policies created by the tenant admin.
claims.quote: Environment admins can't edit policies created by the tenant admin.

claims.claim: Environment-level data policies cannot override tenant-wide data policies.
claims.quote: Environment-level data policies can't override tenant-wide data policies.
